title: Glioblastoma Multiforme Differentiation using MR Imaging
author: Małgorzata eska-Matuszewska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jjjckkn

steps.title: Patient preparation and standard MR sequences
steps.instruction: Instruct the patient to keep eyes closed; no sedation or anesthesia is used. Position the patient in a 1.5 T Signa Hdx MR scanner (GE Medical Systems) equipped with a 16‑channel head‑neck‑spine coil. Acquire the following standard sequences before any contrast administration: axial T1‑weighted, axial, coronal and sagittal T2‑weighted, axial FLAIR, diffusion‑weighted imaging (DWI), dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion, and a 3D post‑contrast T1‑weighted series.

steps.title: Dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion
steps.instruction: Perform DSC perfusion using a fast echo‑planar T2*‑weighted gradient‑echo sequence with TR = 1.900 ms, TE = 80 ms, field‑of‑view = 30 cm, matrix = 192 × 128, slice thickness = 8 mm (no gap), and NEX = 1.0. Ten seconds after the start of image acquisition, inject a bolus of gadobutrol (1.0 mol L⁻¹, Gadovist, Bayer Health Care, Germany) at a dose of 0.1 ml kg⁻¹ via a 20‑gauge catheter placed in the ante‑cubital vein using a Medrad automatic injector at 5 ml s⁻¹, followed immediately by 20 ml saline at the same rate. Continue acquiring images for a total of 1 min 26 s, obtaining sets from 13 axial slices before, during, and after contrast injection. After the perfusion run, acquire a post‑contrast 3D T1‑weighted sequence using the same contrast bolus; no additional contrast is given before DSC imaging.

steps.title: Diffusion‑weighted imaging
steps.instruction: Acquire DWI with a transverse single‑shot echo‑planar sequence using TE = 89.9 ms, TR = 8000 ms, slice thickness = 5 mm, field‑of‑view = 26 cm, matrix = 128 × 128, NEX = 1, diffusion‑sensitizing gradient b = 1000 s mm⁻² applied in three orthogonal directions; total scan time is 42 seconds.

steps.title: Image post‑processing
steps.instruction: Process the perfusion (PWI) and diffusion (DWI) image sets using Functool software (ADW 4.4, GE Medical Systems).

steps.title: ROI placement and perfusion calculations
steps.instruction: On CBV maps fused with post‑contrast T1‑weighted images (for the enhancing tumor core) or with T2‑weighted images (for the peritumoral T2‑hyperintense non‑enhancing zone), place large irregular freehand ROIs outlining the region of interest on each slice. Compute mean rCBV, mean rPH, and mean rPSR as the arithmetic average of all voxel values within the large ROI. Then place small circular ROIs of 40–60 mm² over the hottest spots inside the large ROI on each slice; record the highest values as max rCBV, max rPH, and max rPSR. Avoid inclusion of hemorrhage, necrosis, or large vessels. Normalize all CBV, PH, and PSR values to the values obtained from normal‑appearing white matter of the contralateral hemisphere to obtain relative parameters (rCBV, rPH, rPSR). Calculate PH and PSR from the perfusion curves using the formulas: PH = S0 − Smin, where S0 is the start of contrast passage and Smin is the maximal drop of magnetic susceptibility; PSR = (S1 − Smin) / PH, where S1 is the signal measured 24 seconds after Smin.

substeps.instruction: Define tumor core (enhancing part on CBV map fused with post‑contrast T1) and peritumoral zone (T2‑hyperintense non‑enhancing area on CBV map fused with T2).
Draw large freehand ROI on each slice; compute mean rCBV, rPH, rPSR.
Draw small ROI (40–60 mm²) on hot spots; record maximal rCBV, rPH, rPSR.
Normalize to contralateral normal‑appearing white matter.
Apply PH = S0 − Smin and PSR = (S1 − Smin)/PH (S1 measured 24 s after Smin).

steps.title: ADC measurement
steps.instruction: On the ADC maps derived from the DWI data, manually outline the entire enhancing tumor core on each slice, avoiding areas of hemorrhage or necrosis, and calculate the mean ADC as the arithmetic average of all voxels within the large ROI. Place small ROIs of 40–60 mm² inside the large ROI to obtain the minimum ADC; select the lowest value as min ADC. For hyperperfused tumors, repeat the same ROI strategy in the peritumoral non‑enhancing T2‑hyperintense zone to obtain mean ADC and min ADC values for that region.
